html:
The Gugu Badhun are an Aboriginal Australian nation of the upper Burdekin River in north Queensland, about 220 kilometres northwest of Townsville. Their country includes the small township of Greenvale and a number of cattle stations.

Ludwig Leichhardt passed down the Burdekin and named it in 1845, and squatters took the valley in the 1860s. Their neighbours were the Nyawaygi and Warrgamay toward the coast and the Dyirbal of the rainforest. Many Gugu Badhun families kept working on the stations of their own country through the twentieth century.
